claims.statement: A commutative $K$-algebra $A$ with $K$-derivations $\partial_1,\partial_2,\partial_3,\partial_t$, a $K$-module $B$, a $K$-linear map $I:A\to B$ and a map $D_t:B\to B$ such that $I(\partial_k f)=0$ for all $k,f$ and $I(\partial_t f)=D_t(If)$.
claims.title: Periodic setting, \texttt{PeriodicSetting}

claims.statement: $A=R[\mathbb{Z}^3]$ (finite sums $\sum_n f_n e^{2\pi i n\cdot x}$, $f_n\in R$), where $R$ is a commutative $\mathbb{C}$-algebra with a derivation $D$. Set $\partial_k(\sum f_n e_n)=\sum 2\pi i n_k f_n e_n$, $\partial_t(\sum f_n e_n)=\sum D(f_n)e_n$, $I(f)=f_0$, $D_t=D$.
claims.title: Trigonometric model, \texttt{Trig.setting}

claims.statement: $\partial_k$ and $\partial_t$ are derivations of $R[\mathbb{Z}^3]$.
claims.title: \texttt{dx}, \texttt{dt}

claims.statement: $I(\partial_k f)=2\pi i\cdot 0\cdot f_0=0$ and $I(\partial_t f)=D(f_0)=D(If)$.
claims.title: Torus divergence lemma, \texttt{integral\_dx}, \texttt{integral\_dt}

claims.statement: $u_k\partial_k g=\partial_k(u_k g)-(\partial_k u_k)g$. Hence (\texttt{int\_adv\_eq\_zero}) if (\ref{div}) holds, $I(u_k\partial_k g)=0$.
claims.title: \texttt{adv\_eq}

claims.statement: $\omega_i\partial_k\partial_k\omega_i=\partial_k(\omega_i\partial_k\omega_i)-\partial_k\omega_i\,\partial_k\omega_i$.
claims.title: \texttt{wLapW\_eq}

claims.statement: $2\,\omega_i\,u_k\partial_k\omega_i=u_k\partial_k|\omega|^2$.
claims.title: \texttt{two\_w\_adv}

claims.statement: $\omega_i\omega_j\partial_ju_i=\omega\cdot(\omega\cdot\nabla)u$.
claims.title: \texttt{stretch\_eq}

claims.title: Identity (2), \texttt{weighted\_identity}, \texttt{weighted\_identity\_T3}

claims.statement: $A$ is the algebra of $f\in C^\infty(\mathbb{R}\times\mathbb{R}^3,\mathbb{R})$, $f=f(t,a,b,c)$, with $f(p+e_k)=f(p)$ for the unit spatial vectors $e_1,e_2,e_3$. $\partial_k f(p)=Df(p)e_k$, $\partial_tf(p)=Df(p)e_t$, $I(f)(t)=\int_0^1\!\int_0^1\!\int_0^1 f(t,a,b,c)\,dc\,db\,da$, $D_t=\frac{d}{dt}$.
claims.title: \texttt{Smooth.A}, \texttt{Smooth.setting}

claims.statement: If $F,\partial_sF$ are jointly continuous on $\mathbb{R}\times\mathbb{R}$, then $\frac{d}{ds}\int_0^1F(s,x)\,dx=\int_0^1\partial_sF(s,x)\,dx$.
claims.title: \texttt{Torus.hasDerivAt\_integral01}

claims.statement: If $f,\partial_tf$ are jointly continuous, then $\frac{d}{dt}\int_{\mathbb{T}^3}f=\int_{\mathbb{T}^3}\partial_tf$.

claims.statement: The smooth model is a periodic setting. Hence identities (1) and (2) hold for all $u,\omega,\phi\in A$ satisfying (\ref{div})--(\ref{wt}).

claims.statement: Take $u,\omega,S\in L^2(\mathbb{T}^3)$ whose Fourier coefficients are those of a divergence-free velocity, its curl, and $S=\frac12(\nabla u+\nabla u^T)$. Then $\sum_{ij}\|S_{ij}\|_2^2=\frac12\sum_i\|\omega_i\|_2^2$, so $\|S\|_2\le\|\omega\|_2$.
claims.title: \texttt{Fourier.L2\_strain\_eq}, \texttt{Fourier.L2\_strain\_le}

claims.title: \texttt{Lyapunov.dS\_identity\_smooth}

claims.statement: Let $h,M$ be continuous, $g(0)=0$, and $g'=h\le M^2$ on $[0,t]$. Then $g(t)\le\int_0^tM^2$.
claims.title: \texttt{Lyapunov.le\_integral\_sq\_of\_deriv}
